data.explanation_txt:
Let \(S_{n} \) and \(S'_{n} \) be the sums of n terms of two A.P.'s and \(T_{11} \) and \(T'_{11} \) be the respective \(11^{th} \) terms, then:

\[\cfrac{S_{n} }{S'_{n} } =\cfrac{\cfrac{n}{2} [2a+(n-1)d]}{\cfrac{n}{2} [2a'+(n-1)d']} =\cfrac{7n+1}{4n+27} \]

\[\Rightarrow \cfrac{a+\cfrac{(n-1)}{2} d}{a'+\cfrac{(n-1)}{2} d'} =\cfrac{7n+1}{4n+27} \]

Now put \(n=21\), we get:

\(\cfrac{a+10d}{a'+10d'} =\cfrac{T_{11} }{T'_{11} } =\cfrac{148}{111} =\cfrac{4}{3} \).

Note : If ratio of sum of \(n\) terms of two A.P.'s are given in terms of \(n\) and ratio of their \(p^{th} \) terms are to be found then put \(n=2p-1\). Here we put \(n=11\times 2-1=21\).

data.question_title: Very closely associated with the beauty of the mountains are same special emotions, which the highest and wildest peaks provoke. The companionship provided by climbing together is almost universally valued by mountaineers. Lonely though the mountains peaks are, the teams of mountaineers who climb them find a unique kind of bond developing between them. The friendship established in the mountains are lasting and irreplaceable when you have walked the feather edge of danger with someone, when you have held his hand in your hand, you have an almost impregnable foundation for friendship. For the deepest friendships spring from sharing failure as well as success, danger as well as safety.
